steps.text: Line one defines the prediction function. It receives the current game state, the demonstration rows, and a default neighbor count of nine.
Line two converts the visible game situation into the same four-number sensor vector used by every training example.
Lines three through five measure the squared distance from the current vector to every demonstration, sort from nearest to farthest, and keep the closest nine.
Line six creates one empty vote bucket for LEFT, STAY, and RIGHT. The keys minus one, zero, and one are the three possible actions.
Line seven gives each neighbor an inverse-distance vote. Closer examples count more, and the small constant prevents division by zero on an exact match.
Line eight sorts the three actions by their accumulated vote and returns the strongest one as the agent's next move.
The closing brace ends the function. One sensor state has now become one inspectable action.
